knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Diluting a fresh batch at label strength gives the correct concentration. Adding concentrate to an existing bucket (option 0) over-doses and is named as a common error, and a weak mix (option 2) under-doses and leads to rework.

Only the volume needed is mixed, to reduce waste and the number of unlabelled leftovers. A fixed amount on the label (option 0) and end-of-day mixing being cheaper (option 2) are not the reasons the lesson gives.
The lesson says pour-by-eye is the most common source of error.

practicalCriteria: Learner confirms the dilution from the label or approved procedure before mixing, and states the figure to the assessor.
Learner measures product with a graduated container or the approved dispensing system, not by eye, and does not top up a dilution with concentrate.
Learner labels the mixed container with product, dilution and date, and mixes only the volume needed for the work area.
Learner records any rework from dosing or technique with its cause and the corrective action.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Dosing log, or record of dispensing system checks where used
Rework record with job, cause and corrective action
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses a dilution that does not match the label or approved procedure
Learner uses an unlabelled mixed container
